title: Shortcut Conflict shown when there's no documented conflict.
author: gungfujoe
summary: PowerToys reports Win+Shift+C as a system shortcut conflict even though Color Picker still receives it and the linked Windows documentation does not identify that chord.

status.label: Design investigation ready
status.detail: The current reproduction and detector implementation are specific enough for code investigation.

next_action.label: Investigate conflict attribution
next_action.reason: Distinguish reserved system hotkeys from other registration failures and avoid unsupported ownership claims.

judgment.rationale: The issue is current, reproducible, narrowly scoped, and repository inspection identifies the detector and attribution path.
evidence: Win+Shift+C is reported as a system conflict on 0.101.2362.
Color Picker continues to work with the chord.
The linked Windows shortcut reference has no matching entry.
judgment.recommended_action: Continue focused design for conflict probing, attribution, and wording; do not expose approve_design until implementation-grade.

issue_context.summary: The conflict detector labels a functioning Color Picker chord as a Windows system conflict and links documentation that does not support the classification.
known_information: PowerToys displays one conflict attributed to a system shortcut.
No duplicate, assignee, or linked fix is present.
inferences: RegisterHotKey failure may mean a system reservation or another application; the probe cannot identify the owner.
Color Picker may use an activation path different from the registration probe.
issue_context.analysis: More user diagnostics are unnecessary: current code converts a registration failure directly into the stronger claim that the system owns the shortcut.
initial_investigation: hotkey_conflict_detector.cpp::HasConflictWithSystemHotkey uses RegisterHotKey and treats ERROR_HOTKEY_ALREADY_REGISTERED as system conflict.
GetAllConflicts synthesizes an owner named System.
The detector has no owner identity, so the UI link can overstate the evidence.
Issue search found no separate Win+Shift+C duplicate.
